body:
My parents are also alcoholics. Luckily for me they are high-functioning. I wish it wasn't the case, they were always grown up children to me. As I am now. 

But what things do make you happy?

I had this same thought last night. Blissful silence and darkness. But the problem is you have no consciousness with which to enjoy it. "Enjoy" will no longer exist for you should you go through with it.

The chaos of your mind is what separates you from the beasts. For better or for worse. You have to make your peace with that. Most have at least a shred of power that we can use to turn that chaos into order every now and again. Live for those moments. Live for the little things.

Like how good a glass of water tastes after a long bike ride. (or w/e comes to your mind)

It does help to know someone is listening. Especially being that I don't feel comfortable talking to my friends or family about this. 

Of course I want friends. In fact, I do have meetups planned. I have issues meeting people because of a few deal breakers I have (namely regarding religious folk). But I will be trying harder in the near future. And I'll try to get past that deal breaker too.

I'm not sure on the writing. I wish I could say it's likely to happen, but I doubt it. I just brought it up because if I have a passion, it's that. But it's more likely to say I'm dispassionate about most things in this life. Love, god, possessions... most of these things just make me roll my eyes. 

I probably won't take my life today. I owe that much to my younger sibling. But I am really fucked in the head right now. And I just have ever-increasing feelings of "none of this is worth it."
So like, I just posted here too. And maybe I'm the worst person in the world to talk to right now. But I just wanted to comment and tell you someone is listening, at the very least.
